h1: Khanom Beach Resort & Spa — a small beachfront hideaway on quiet Nadan Beach
intro: Khanom is Nakhon Si Thammarat's Gulf-coast shoreline — still quiet, white-sand, and home to the famous pink dolphins — and Khanom Beach Resort & Spa is a small resort that opened in 2019 sitting right on Nadan Beach, just steps from the sand. With only 31 rooms and villas, from Deluxe Garden View up to a 123 sqm Private Pool Villa, it stays private and unhurried · Free bikes and kayaks, and staff who remember your name · From approx. ฿4,500/night · Scores 8.5 from 45 reviews.

body.html: Khanom Beach Resort & Spa is a small resort that opened in 2019 on Nadan Beach in Khanom district — its appeal is simple and clear: a beachfront location and genuine quiet · Khanom itself is a Gulf-coast shoreline that sees far fewer visitors than the Andaman side, with white sand, fairly clear water, and pink-dolphin tours as the area's signature draw · With only 31 rooms and villas, the atmosphere stays private and never feels crowded like a big resort.

Rooms come in several tiers — Deluxe Garden View and Sea View at 46 sqm, which is genuinely spacious for the price, up to a 58 sqm Garden Villa and a 123 sqm Private Pool Villa with its own pool · Many reviews praise the roomy layouts, large bathrooms with a clear separated wet area, and well-equipped rooms, with some featuring an in-room jacuzzi · Decor is understated but smart, and cleanliness — both in the rooms and the public areas — is one of the things guests mention most.
"So quiet and private. You walk from the room to the pool and straight on to the beach. Staff were lovely and remembered us, and the free bikes to ride around were a nice touch."

The heart of the resort is the outdoor infinity pool facing Nadan Beach, with the resort's own stretch of sand just beyond it · There is a spa for massages, the Bella Luna restaurant open from morning to night, and a beachfront Luna Bar · What guests like most are the freebies — bikes, kayaks, and buffet breakfast — which make the stay feel better value · The leafy gardens are pleasant to wander, suiting travellers who want to slow down rather than chase busy activities.

To be honest, the main thing to accept is that in-resort dining is on the pricey side — several reviews note the restaurant costs more than you'd expect for Khanom, so eating every meal here adds up · Garden-view rooms can also pick up the sound of frogs and insects from the gardens on some nights, which is charming to some and a nuisance to others · And poolside service can be a touch slow on busy days — common at a small resort that doesn't run a large staff.

On getting there: Khanom sits at the far north of Nakhon Si Thammarat, on the border with Surat Thani — roughly 1.5–2 hours by car from Nakhon Si Thammarat city, and close to Khanom pier with boats to Koh Samui and Koh Phangan · Flying into Samui (USM) or Surat Thani (URT) and driving over is more convenient than flying into Nakhon · The area around the resort is quiet with few restaurants outside the property, so a car or rental is handy · It scores 8.5 from 45 reviews on Trip.com and 4.8/5 on TripAdvisor, ranked #1 of 20 hotels in Khanom — a clearly positive trend.

Honestly, Khanom Beach Resort isn't for everyone · If you want a central in-town base with restaurants and shops within walking distance, or a large activity-packed resort, this isn't it · But if you're after a quiet beachfront stay on a coast that hasn't been overrun — waking up to the sea, riding a bike, paddling a kayak, and heading out to see pink dolphins — Khanom is the answer, and this is one of the best-run places on the beach · It suits couples, families, and small groups who genuinely want to unwind.

A tip from reading the reviews: if your budget allows, step up to a Sea View room or Garden Villa — better value than garden view, with the full atmosphere and away from the night-time frog chorus · Plan a few meals outside the resort to keep the food budget in check · And book the early-morning pink-dolphin tour through the resort in advance, as it's the Khanom highlight you shouldn't miss.

honestChecks: If you want to keep food costs down — the in-resort menu runs pricey for Khanom → plan some meals at restaurants outside, or keep a car to drive into Khanom town for food.
If you're a light sleeper — garden-view rooms can pick up frogs and insects on some nights → step up to a Sea View room or Garden Villa, which is quieter and gives you the full beach atmosphere.
If you don't have your own car — Khanom is 1.5–2 hours from Nakhon city with few shops nearby → rent a car, use the resort's transfer service, and book tours through the resort in advance.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Khanom Beach Resort & Spa

faq.q: Where is Khanom Beach Resort & Spa, and how do I get there?
faq.a: It sits directly on Nadan Beach in Khanom district, Nakhon Si Thammarat, with a private beach in front · Khanom is at the far north of the province on the Surat Thani border, about 1.5–2 hours by car from Nakhon city · Flying into Samui (USM) or Surat Thani (URT) and driving over is more convenient than flying into Nakhon · It's near Khanom pier with boats to Koh Samui and Koh Phangan.

faq.q: What does Khanom Beach Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿4,500/night for a 46 sqm Deluxe Garden View · Stepping up there's Deluxe Sea View, a 58 sqm Garden Villa, and a 123 sqm Private Pool Villa with its own pool · Prices vary by season and rise in high season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Khanom Beach Resort best for?
faq.a: It's best for couples, families, and small groups who want a quiet beachfront stay on Khanom's still-uncrowded coast · You get a private beach, an infinity pool, and freebies like bikes and kayaks · It's not ideal if you want a central in-town base within walking distance of shops, or a big activity-packed resort.

faq.q: What is there to do in Khanom — can you see pink dolphins?
faq.a: Khanom is home to pink dolphins, and the dolphin tour is the area's highlight — early-morning departures give the best chance to spot them · There are also Nai Plao Beach, Nadan Beach, viewpoints, and nearby islands · The resort can arrange tours and transfers, so book ahead.

faq.q: What's the dining like — is it expensive?
faq.a: The Bella Luna restaurant is open from morning to night, with a beachfront Luna Bar too · Several reviews note that in-resort dining is on the pricey side for Khanom, so eating every meal here adds up · Keeping a car to drive into Khanom town for some meals helps control the budget.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: With only 31 rooms and villas, high season (December–March) and long weekends fill quickly, so book 1–2 months ahead, especially for the private pool villas · Other times 2–3 weeks is enough · Every platform offers Free Cancellation — choose that if plans aren't firm, and compare a few sites before confirming.
